claims.claim: The game lacks any instructions, tutorial, or guidance on core survival mechanics and controls.

citations.review_text:
This game can be best summarised in a single picture. The tooltip, which shows two non-distinct square buttons, on the left side "RMB" and on the right side, "LMB". Could have given them mouse-button looking icons. Could have not have them fucking flipped. But no.

A game advertised as being past the final chapter, yet pre-early access levels of neglect to detail and general yank. No tutorial, which can be fun, since it is a survival game where you have to follow your intuition. The UI ensures you do exactly the opposite of what you want to do, though. "pick up" means you demolish your farm and destroy all your crops. You will drink salt water without hesitation upon rmb but it takes 2 seconds of holding lmb without any animation to pour it out. 

When a shark attacks, you might want to switch to your weapon immediately, but that's not allowed, you have slowly reel in whatever you were holding with your hook until the shark finished eating your boat.

Anchors are single use because fuck you thats why.

(Initial Impressions) So far its a nope from me.
- This could be a good game and has a lot of potential but.. On first play feels more like an alpha than any kind of even half finished release.

- Firstly the controls don't follow the standard rules properly on things like item control and then there are no instructions or tutorial - none at all. I did eventually manage to eat but its a clumsy process. (was saved by Google search) There is no way to eat or drink things directly from your inventory - no use button or anything like it.

- This is the second and the real kicker on food - food only lasts seconds then you will be back to fighting starvation again. Food levels seem to go down faster than water. In a survival game real realism is impossible but just a little bit can go a long way. 

- While on the raft you have a grappling hook but using it tends to have you in the water very quickly. Then the shark will have you. It will also soon eat your tiny raft. You get to an island and swim ashore (if the shark doesn't get you on the way). Then you discover that your grappling hook can't grapple even a tiny raft so that is rapidly lost.

- Once on your tiny island you can survive for a short time but will soon discover that the food is very limited. Also once there overnight you will find that you are getting no more debris to grab from the sea so building anything is impossible and starvation is inevitable. 

So far more a slow death simulator than a survival simulator..

There are literally no instructions to be seen whatsoever. Nothing is intuitive, and an hour and a half into the game you're left wondering if there is ever a point that feels like fun. Played with my GF, the two of us together could barely make any progress at all, and were stressed and confused the entire time. Not exactly what one would call "A fun game"

Which most of us controller users don't know that INSTANTLY REFUNDING IT!!!!

Anchors are single use because fuck you thats why.

I know we all hate super hand-holdy games but this goes so far in the opposite direction it's not even fun. There are many unintuitive mechanics/design choices that your only real option to understand how to play is to watch some videos on how to play. Incredibly lazy decisions made by the developer, I would not buy this game at regular price or even half price. It's also quite a hostile experience trying to play with a controller, so don't even bother. I'm sure it'll get better but everything feels so stiff and clunky - this is not a game that feels good to play, maybe it feels good to overcome... I'm getting a refund though and maybe I'll give it another go if it dips below $5.

I'm glad I caught myself before the 2 hour refund limit because some of the other reviews speak to issues that I wouldn't discover unless going much deeper into the game. If the controls weren't stiff and clunky, and they took 10 minutes to explain the basic mechanics of managing your raft (my first game I went to check out an island, my raft floated away, resources in the water despawned when my raft left, and I didn't have enough resources to build a new one, didn't know things could only be built on the raft, etc ,etc.)

It's also far to easy too die and far too punishing when you do, so the game itself doesn't even encourage learning how to play by playing. Maybe it's more fun if you have 4 people to gather resources, stab boars, and manage a single raft - but for me this was just 2 hours of my life wasted and filled with frustration.
For the short time I played this it seemed very boring and grindy. Extremely slow paced and very janky controls. Only would recommend if you play with a lot of friends.

I love the idea of survival games and building a raft/boat up from scavenge.
Raft looked great from the outside but disappointed me. It quickly turns into a repetitive slog, and the long-term rewards to keep playing felt poorer and poorer the more I kept going.
At first it's fun but the game play becomes boring and repetitive really quickly, the story is extremely uncompelling it completely ruins the game for me.

i found an island and did not know mobs could spawn on land, after getting on shore and dying to a fucking boar, i lose some my items and tried to find them only to realize you lose items for good when you die. also the mob just teleported to me. i checked to see if it was close by and saw it on the other side of the isle only to die a second later. this game sucks and is repetitive. fuck this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game offers cooperative multiplayer allowing players to build and customize their own rafts together.

citations.review_text: Very good survival game with coop its even better and chill!

Raft will immerse you in a thrilling, exciting world, whether you're playing solo or with friends.

It’s a world completely submerged in water, leaving behind only the tips of islands and countless floating scraps of materials that will help you survive.

You can easily spend dozens of hours with your friends or other players in co-op mode. There are hundreds of raft customization ideas, a hundred different decor items, and an endless stream of new islands waiting along your path.

Raft also features its own storyline, where the ultimate goal is to escape this sunken world—either on your own or alongside your crew.

I bought Raft on sale because my older sister already had it in her Steam library. And yeah, we played the entire time together, just the two of us. Those memories, the funny and unforgettable moments, will stay with me as something uniquely ours. I’ll be looking back on those times with a smile on my face for a long time to come, even after my sister moves to live in another country.

If you enjoy survival games, building, and engaging mechanics, you already know where to go.

Good luck escaping the flooded world.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the hunger and thirst meters as depleting much too fast, requiring constant management.

citations.review_text:
One of the most boring games I've ever played (long playtime only because my friend likes it).

1. Insanely boring gameplay. You literally just spend hours and hours collecting trash from the ocean.
2. Pretty much zero storyline. The notes you find mean absolutely nothing.
3. Extremely annoying controls, and you're constantly running out of food and water. Preparing food takes so much time that it's easier to just die.
4. And that's pretty much it. You just waste your time torturing yourself with this game without getting anything in return. No relaxation, no fun, no story progression, no sense of achievement, no satisfaction.

Sorry for being so blunt, but I honestly can't think of a single good thing to say about this game.
Game is good but why the fuck do you always need to drink and eat omd, i get full bars that only last 5 mins

About 30h in and i’ve had a blast but hit a wall.

It’s get very repetative fast after early game. 

I’ve also got a thing for food and water bars that deplete WAY to fast. It’s not a survival mechanic at that point it’s just anoying.

You can go 2-3 days without water and weeks without out food but somehow i need 5 steaks a day not to die of starvation? I get it would be redundant if it was realistic but some games skew it way to hard. And Raft is ome of those games. 

The islands are pretty empty apart from story islands and it gets very repetative after a while. 

Still a good 30h and all but i’m done

claims.claim: Reviewers note that achievements require excessive repetitive grinding or save-scumming and exploits to complete.

citations.review_text:
For Normal Players:

100% get this game me and my friends beat the story in around 20 hours playing for fun building our raft and experimenting with all the items and exploring the items. The game we found was kind of buggy with saves not saving, getting randomly kicked, falling inside the islands and buggy hitboxes but over all would recommened getting this game to play with friends


People wanting 100% the game:

For your sanity DO NOT this is not worth the nearly 100 hours one has to do to complete this as pretty much all the acheivements are "Kill 1 of X", "Kill 50 of X", then KILL 50 OF X" this is ridiculous there is no skill involved for these acheivements and are there just to keep people playing but they arent the worst as pretty much all the acheivements can be obtained from save scummung but the survive 365 day acheivement is what kept me and my friends on the longest with our computers being left on all day and night as we have completed every other acheivement luckily I didn't have to stay on long as my friend was hosting the server and when I joined again the acheivement popped (Thankfully) but if you want to 100% this game for the sake of yourself DON'T!

A fun base (raft) building, resource collecting grind. I find the gameplay loop, resource management, etc. very enjoyable! 

The achievements are only really feasible if you keep reloading saves to grind out some hard/time-consuming kills, and use a few exploits. It's either that-- or play for at least a hundred hours.

For Normal Players:

The game we found was kind of buggy with saves not saving, getting randomly kicked, falling inside the islands and buggy hitboxes but over all would recommened getting this game to play with friends


People wanting 100% the game:

For your sanity DO NOT this is not worth the nearly 100 hours one has to do to complete this as pretty much all the acheivements are "Kill 1 of X", "Kill 50 of X", then KILL 50 OF X" this is ridiculous there is no skill involved for these acheivements and are there just to keep people playing but they arent the worst as pretty much all the acheivements can be obtained from save scummung but the survive 365 day acheivement is what kept me and my friends on the longest with our computers being left on all day and night as we have completed every other acheivement luckily I didn't have to stay on long as my friend was hosting the server and when I joined again the acheivement popped (Thankfully) but if you want to 100% this game for the sake of yourself DON'T!

It's a good game, but still sooo janky... The main difficulty comes from fighting the UI instead of dealing with things in the game.

The controls have multiple buttons do things that should be the same button. This will constantly make you do the wrong action, like drinking saltwater instead of placing it in a purifier. It does at least clearly display what the controls do, but it's a pain to be constantly reviewing them each action to make sure I don't kill myself again.

It won't let you switch from a tool that's deployed, like the hook or fishing pole, so when you're panicking trying to pull out a spear to defend yourself it will do nothing. It should automatically reel up the tool then switch to the next weapon.

It still doesn't automatically pull supplies from nearby chests when crafting, a quality of life staple in these sorts of games. So you get to endlessly open chests trying to find the one thing you left in an smart place.

Things clip through each other all the time. You'll park your raft by an island, go explore it, then find your raft ghosted through the island and left you, with the shark swimming across the land to chase it. Or you'll watch items clip through your hook you are trying to reel in.

It won't let you pause in solo games unless you turn off the network code when loading the game, leading to lots of reloads when I find I stepped away and find myself dead when I come back.

Sure, the incredibly janky UI contributes to the survival feeling of the game, but not in a good way. I've already bought many copies of the game and I'm glad to see indie devs making such epic games, but please give it a little more polish.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players find the combat encounters simple and glitchy.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe combat as overly simple, unresponsive, and glitchy, leading many to avoid it entirely.

citations.review_text:
I have a complicated relationship with Raft. On one hand, I like the concept. Building a raft from nothing, surviving off scraps, making every encounter with solid land count as much as you can. Gathering every single resource and holding onto just in case. The idea of a flooded world is great! The building is fun, the exploration is nice.... For a while. 
And I think that's the end of the nice things I have to say about Raft. The actual gameplay loop is so mind numbingly dull and repetitive that at a certain point the "engaging" methods of gathering resources get so annoying that you just ignore them entirely. Why stop at an small island to get wood when you can just sit on the boat and gather random bullshit with nets. Why hook things in at all (wasting durablity on your tools) when you can just jump out and eat the damage of the shark to grab what you want? Why cook anything when a few island in you can just grab vending machine coins (THAT RESPAWN) and buy food for basically free? Why do combat at all (it's painfully unresponsive, glitchy, and just bad) when you can just ignore it. Just don't get hit stupid. 
The story is almost interesting, but I say almost because I still don't really know what it is beyond Olof is bad, world flooded, stop Olof I guess. The "boss fights" suck, plain and simple. The end-game items and upgrades are so laughably pointless, you get the good gear at the end of the game when there's literally no reason left to play after you find the blueprints unless you're going for the 356 day achievement. 
This game has a lot going for it, and a lot more taking away from it. It's more fun with friends when you can break up chores together, but alone it's a miserable slog where you always seem to be struggling to catch up with something. 
And, I cannot state this enough, enemies respawn so fast it's not even funny. Kill the seagull that's eating your crops? It's back within less than a minute. Good luck keeping your flowers for the beehives to cr…

“Raft™ throws you and your friends into an epic oceanic adventure! Alone or together, players battle to survive a perilous voyage across a vast sea!”

--Gameplay: 7/10

What sets Raft apart from most other survival games is its approach to the base-building mechanic. As the name implies, your raft is your base. Not only that, but it also serves as your means of travel through the endless ocean. With this approach, the game essentially eliminates the backtracking that you would normally have to do after long trips in other games. 

Expanding your raft, upgrading it with proper navigation and engines, and watching it slowly become a proper self-sustaining vessel is a very rewarding experience. It is further reinforced by the many decoration options available to you, allowing you to fully customize it to your liking.

Combat, however, in this game is a different story. It is overly simple and easy, poses no real threat, and offers no challenge or player engagement. Enemies usually have one or two attacks that are easily avoided, often not requiring more than two steps to the side. Because of this, combat encounters become a nuisance very soon and are ultimately best avoided, especially since there are no worthwhile rewards.

Resource gathering can be quite a slow process, and paired with most crafting recipes requiring a high material cost, Raft can often feel grindy and slow, even with multiple players.

After finishing your daily errands and the maintenance required to keep your vessel operating, you might often find yourself stuck out in the ocean with nothing to do but wait. That is a drawback of having a floating base out in the ocean, since downtime becomes considerably more boring. You will sit and wait to reach the next island, wait for floating debris to drift your way so you can collect materials and build, or just wait for various production tasks to finish.

Exploration outside the story islands is sadly quite bland. Other than the story islands, the island…

single_points.text: One reviewer says that the game really should have a good built-in tutorial and has nothing like that.

citation.review_text:
After only 4 hours of play, I can tell you that this is not an easy game to learn, but it looks like it will be worth the  effort required. I'm not sorry that I bought it and I expect that I will get fair value for my money.

One criticism is that it really should have a good built-in tutorial and it has nothing like that. I would recommend using Dr. Incompetent's Guide for Beginners on Youtube to get started or you may get so frustrated that you just give up on it.

Fortunately the game has adjustable difficulty levels and you can learn a lot by starting at the easiest settings and waiting to try more challenging levels until you know the basics.

After about 90 hours I nearly gave up at Caravan Island because of the water hose puzzle, which would be quite easy for two people working together but is very difficult if you're solo. Just before I surrendered to frustration I discovered that the lowest hose elbow keeps resetting itself so you have to check that and reset it every time you go back up to try the pump.

So I managed to keep going, now at Tangaroa Island (127 hours) I'm stuck again because the Butler Bots are nowhere to be found and you can't advance without disabling one and stealing its keycard. I found out that this is a known bug that apparently has never been fixed. Players suggest leaving and sailing at least 2000 KM away before returning, which will force a respawn, so I guess I'll try that and maybe visit a few loot islands on the way. It won't be a total waste of time if I can manage to catch a llama along the way, so I can get some wool and open up a few more items.

I still like the game, incidentally, and I would still be glad I bought it even if I can't finish the whole story.

So I left, went back to the Radio Tower, then returned and the Butler Bots had spawned while I was gone so now I can proceed with the game. That's a relief.

Dude, fix ur game man..
My raft has just been swallowed by an island, it actually went inside the island and became one with it. I am completely unable to interact with my raft at all. On top of that, some of my items have fused into the ground and can no longer be picked up. Those were my valuable items, man. they were incredibly hard to get, and now they’ve been swallowed and absorbed into the terrain.
